transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I've been having these thoughts lately. I just keep catching myself thinking that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that, but... those thoughts are there, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, I just quit caring about the things that usually settle me down. Things like fishing, or going out and digging through old vinyl records. Even stuff like tailgating or checking on my home-brew. I don't know, lately they all just feel like chores instead of something fun. I just haven't had any real interest in doing them.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, this low spell has been hanging on for... I'd say about three months now. Yeah, it's been about three months right since that crash.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. I mean, after that burst of energy I had wore off, it just felt like somebody had completely pulled the plug on me. Most of the time now, I just... I'll sit at the kitchen table staring at my coffee. I just feel completely empty. And ashamed, honestly. It just kind of stays like that the whole day.
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much or that you're letting others down lately?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I feel pretty empty and tired, like I mentioned, but I don't really sit around feeling worthless or like a burden to anybody. It's just more of a... a total lack of energy and interest, you know? But not that guilty, worthless feeling.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm tired, sure, but I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than normal. And I definitely haven't been restless or pacing around or anything. I just sit there, mostly.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so good that people around you noticed a significant change in your mood or behavior?

Yeah, actually. Right after I got fired, I felt... oddly fired up. I mean, instead of being upset about it, I just felt like I was going to prove everybody wrong. I had a lot of energy then. But it wasn't just a good feeling, I was also pretty on edge. I remember snapping at people over little things down at the coffee shop. So, yeah, people probably noticed I was acting different.
How long did that unusually energetic or 'fired up' period last after you got fired?
It lasted about three weeks. Yeah, that whole high-energy, kind of out-of-control stretch went on for about three weeks right after I lost the job.

During that time when you felt unusually energetic or 'fired up,' did you also feel like your thoughts were racing, or did you find yourself doing things that were out of character for you, like spending a lot of money, taking on big projects, or acting impulsively?

Yeah, my mind was definitely racing. It was like... my thoughts were just jumping around so fast. One second I'd be running through my old sales numbers, and then right into new job leads, and then suddenly I'm thinking about beer recipes, or getting mad over old arguments I had years ago. I just couldn't keep hold of one idea for more than a few seconds before it was on to the next thing.

During that time when you felt unusually energetic and your thoughts were racing, did you also experience a noticeably elevated or irritable mood, such as feeling unusually confident, happy, or easily annoyed, for a distinct period of time?

Yeah, I was definitely feeling unusually confident. I mean, for a while there, I honestly believed I could just walk into any store in the district and run it better than the managers they had. It was like... like losing my job had somehow made me the expert. I just felt like I knew better than everyone else.

During that time when you felt unusually energetic and overly confident, was there a clear period where your mood was noticeably elevated or irritable — like you were feeling unusually good or agitated — that was different from your usual self?

Yeah, it was definitely different from my usual self. Right after I got fired, I felt oddly fired up... like I was just going to prove everybody wrong. I felt really good about it, honestly. But I was also getting agitated pretty easily. Like, I remember snapping at people over little things at the coffee shop, stuff that wouldn't normally bother me. So yeah, it was this mix of feeling really driven but also just really irritable.
During that time when you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, and irritable, did your mood stay elevated or agitated for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four consecutive days?

Yeah, it definitely lasted longer than four days. That whole high-energy, out-of-control stretch... it went on for about three weeks right after I was fired. It was just day after day of feeling like that.
During that time when you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, and irritable, did you need less sleep than usual, such as feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep?

Yeah, I definitely didn't need much sleep back then. There were several nights where I think I only slept two, maybe three hours. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all. I'd get up feeling like I had a full tank of gas and just... no reason to slow down. I was ready to go the second I woke up.

During that time when you felt so energetic and confident, did you find yourself doing things much more quickly or intensely than usual, like starting multiple projects at once, rushing around, or feeling like you couldn't sit still?

Yeah, definitely. I just couldn't really sit still. I was bouncing from filling out job applications to... well, sketching out these woodworking projects, and then I'd jump right over to rewriting my resume. I was hardly sitting in one place long enough to actually finish one thing before I was already starting the next.

During that time when you felt so energetic and confident, did you also find yourself talking more than usual, having trouble focusing on just one thing, or taking on risky or unusual projects that you wouldn't normally consider?

Yeah, I was definitely talking a lot more. I remember being at the park, at the chess tables, and... well, I was telling everyone about my big plan to bounce back after losing my job. I just couldn't stop talking. People actually kept telling me to take a breath because the words were just pouring out of me. Once I started, I just kept going.

During that time when you felt unusually energetic, confident, and irritable, did you also experience at least three other changes like being more talkative, having racing thoughts, being easily distracted, having an increased goal-directed activity, or engaging in risky or pleasurable activities that you wouldn’t usually do?

Yeah, along with the talking and the projects, my mind was definitely racing. My thoughts were just jumping so fast from my old retail sales numbers to new job leads, and then over to, like, beer recipes, and then suddenly I'd be thinking about old arguments. I just couldn't keep hold of one idea for more than a few seconds before my brain was already on to the next thing.
Have you ever experienced a time when your mood was so elevated or irritable that it caused problems in your life, like affecting your relationships, work, or judgment?

Yeah, it definitely caused some problems. Because I was bouncing around so much, I ended up falling behind on my bills. I'd miss callbacks for jobs, completely forget about appointments... I just couldn't keep a steady job search going, even though I really needed the work. And things at home just got sloppy. My usual routines were out the window. It got to the point where I realized I couldn't just handle it all by sheer willpower anymore.
